title: Linked List Cycle
prompt:
Return `true` if the linked list has a cycle (some node's `next` points back to an earlier node).

Do it in O(1) space with Floyd's tortoise-and-hare: a slow pointer and a fast pointer — if there's a loop, the fast one eventually laps the slow one and they meet.
hints: Picture two runners, one twice as fast as the other. On a straight track the fast one simply reaches the end; on a circular track, what eventually happens?

Slow moves 1 node, fast moves 2. In a cycle, the gap between them shrinks by one each step, so they must land on the same node. Loop guard: `while (fast != null && fast.next != null)` — if fast escapes to null, there's no cycle.
Compare with `==` (same node object, not equal values), and only after moving both: `if (slow == fast) return true;`

solution.explanation: Floyd's tortoise-and-hare. Without a cycle, fast reaches null; with one, once both are inside the loop fast gains one node per step on slow, so it can't jump over it and they meet within one lap. `==` is correct here because we care whether they reference the same node object. O(n) time, O(1) space (a HashSet of visited nodes also works but costs O(n) space).
